excerpt: Use an AED 1 million total budget to compare UAE property strategies, including acquisition costs, reserves and financing.
introduction:
An AED 1 million total investment budget is not the same as an AED 1 million property price. Purchase costs, initial work and a reserve reduce the amount available for the home. If financing is used, future repayments and the lender's valuation must also fit the plan.

No sample allocation below proves that a suitable property is currently available.
takeaways: Set aside charges and a reserve before choosing a price ceiling.
Compare the income and risks of actual units over the same holding period.
Request current listings and written lender and authority quotes before committing.

sections.heading: Allocate the million before viewing
sections.body:
Decide how much of the total must remain accessible for repairs, vacancy and unexpected payments. Estimate purchase expenses and any furnishing or inspection, then calculate the maximum price for a cash purchase. Replace estimates with current written quotes for the actual transaction.

As an illustration, AED 1,000,000 less a sample AED 60,000 for acquisition and work and AED 40,000 reserve leaves AED 900,000 for a cash price. These example amounts show how to divide the total budget between price, costs and a reserve. The amount needed for a real transaction may differ.

sections.heading: Decide what the investment must do
sections.body:
A buyer seeking stable long-term income may prioritise existing leases, an operating building and predictable charges. Someone planning future personal use may value a particular layout, commute or community. Both need the registered right, full costs and an exit plan.

The [RAK area guide](/journal/ras-al-khaimah-property-lifestyle) and [Ajman area guide](/journal/ajman-property-2026) provide contrasting location context. Review specific properties across locations using the same criteria instead of presuming every unit in a named area performs alike.

sections.heading: Cash or mortgage?
sections.body:
A cash purchase avoids ongoing mortgage payments but can tie a large share of capital to one property. Borrowing may preserve liquidity while adding interest, fees, insurance and exposure to changing rates. Compare the full repayment schedule and total cost, not only the initial monthly amount.

The [Central Bank’s 2024 financial stability report](https://www.centralbank.ae/media/p2rpafum/cbuae-fsr-report_2025_en.pdf) describes maximum lending ratios and affordability requirements; lender approval is not automatic. Request written terms and a valuation. A valuation below the purchase price can increase the buyer's required cash contribution.

sections.heading: Compare net income rather than advertised yield
sections.body:
Request recent signed leases for genuinely similar units and note the date, size, condition and furnishing. Deduct vacancy, service charges, insurance, repairs and management from expected rent. Divide annual net operating income by acquisition cost; calculate finance payments separately to estimate cash flow.

As a sensitivity check, model a vacant period and a repair in the same year. Ask who pays utilities during vacancy and whether the building has planned major works. If a property only appears affordable when every month is occupied, the estimate needs more caution.

sections.heading: Compare ready and off-plan commitments
sections.body:
For a ready property, inspect the apartment, common areas and charge statements. If tenanted, review the lease and deposit and verify when the owner can use or re-let it. For off-plan, confirm project registration, signed specification, payment recipient and contractual delivery and delay provisions.

Plot every instalment against available cash and reliable income. The deposit may be a small fraction of the total price, but future milestones are still obligations. Do not rely on an assumed resale before handover to fund payments unless you can meet them if the sale does not happen.

sections.heading: Verify the buyer's legal right
sections.body:
Rules differ by emirate, nationality, entity and designated area. The [UAE government's ownership overview](https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/moving-to-the-uae/expatriates-buying-a-property-in-the-uae) provides a starting point; ask the local authority to confirm the current right for the exact property and buyer. Review title or interim registration, seller authority, mortgages and required clearances.

Obtain a written breakdown of registration, brokerage and other buyer-paid costs. Check payment details independently and keep receipts. A brochure or reservation form does not by itself establish the registered ownership right.

sections.heading: Plan a realistic exit
sections.body:
Seek completed sales of comparable units rather than relying only on asking prices. Note differences in floor, view, size, condition and date, and seek an independent valuation when evidence is limited. Include selling costs, any loan settlement and a period without rent in the proceeds estimate.

Test a lower sale price and a longer sale period against your liquidity needs. A projected return is not a guarantee, and a larger budget does not remove the risk of concentrating capital in one building.

sections.heading: Compare two candidates in writing
sections.body:
Create a one-page worksheet for each property with the same headings: purchase price, buyer-paid acquisition costs, initial work, annual service charges, comparable rent, vacancy, insurance and expected management. Add the date and source of every figure. For a financed candidate, show the bank valuation, initial cash, repayment schedule and remaining balance separately.

An apartment with a lower price can still require more work or have a higher annual charge. A larger property may appeal to a different tenant and take a different time to let. Ask which facts are verified and which are estimates, then test the estimates against less favourable outcomes. Do not treat an agent's asking rent as a completed lease.

Finally, consider concentration: one property exposes much of the budget to a single building, management arrangement and local market. Choose an emergency reserve and holding period that remain suitable even if the expected rent or sale is delayed.

sections.heading: Request current candidates
sections.body:
Browse [Aliyas UAE projects](/projects) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with your total budget, financing preference and intended use. Ask which exact units are currently available and obtain their plans, price, charges and ownership documents.

Recalculate the complete budget from actual quotes before signing. If no suitable unit leaves the required reserve, revise the criteria or wait rather than assuming availability.
